#4062. Nvidia ensure unboxing a ludicrously expensive new graphics card isn't limited to real life in these RAM crisis times by releasing a GeForce 8800 GTX unpacking sim

Hey at least the card in this bit of 2006 nostalgia bait has only cost you a virtual arm and leg

In what feels a fairly cheeky move during a time when memory shortages have infamously made it pretty much impossible to buy a decently powerful new graphics card without spending approximately a gazillion pounds/dollars/dollarpounds, Nvidia have decided to put out a Steam demo that allows folks to re-live the feeling of unboxing a ludicrously expensive graphics card in 2006.

The demo, dubbed GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend, has been developed by Dylan Browne. He previously made Through The Ages, a "real-time high end graphical cinematic that takes us on a nostalgic journey through three of NVIDIA's iconic GPUs" which is also on Steam for reasons.

The GeForce 8800 GTX demo, as you might've guessed, is a tribute to that specific card in the form of a tech demo simulating what it was like to unbox one in a mid-2000s bedroom. Seriously, there's a copy of Crysis on the desk so you know this is the domain of a true devotee to the best graphics available in around 2007.

"Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower," the demo's description declares. "Explore nods to GeForce history and hidden easter eggs as DLSS 4.5 with Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, path tracing, and Mega Geometry bring the nostalgic setting to life. From holding the card to the glow of the monitor, rediscover a moment in PC gaming history - or experience it for the first time!"

As the GeForce 8800 GTX was a top-line card that cost $599 on release in 2006 - about $1,000 in today's money if the online inflation calculator I've just used is on the money - this isn't really a 'we know cards are ludicrously expensive right now, but here's a reminder of when you used to be able to actually afford to unbox one' sort of demo. It is at least a free way to virtually experience having blown a chunk of your savings on something that can render really sexy textures without the existential dread of doing so in real life.

Well, I say that, I've just noticed the minimum requirements for the demo note that you'll need an RTX 4070 card. So, depending on your current setup, this might well be a case of Nvidia offering the chance to render unboxing a card you couldn't afford in 2006 via a card you can't afford in 2026.

Is that about the best we can all hope for in 2026? Probably.

#4061. GTA 6 PS5 Codes Potentially Being Stolen from Physical Copies Using Flashlight Trick

A potentially problematic manufacturing oversight may be resulting in some GTA 6 codes being stolen from retail PS5 cases.

Some reports claim that by pointing a strong flashlight at the side of the case, it’s possible to shine light into the empty Blu-ray box in such a way that it makes the code printed on the insert visible.

Remember, GTA 6’s physical release is a code-in-box, and doesn’t have a Blu-ray disc.

There is some debate about whether the included poster insert blocks the light and makes this impossible; some say they’ve been able to replicate the issue, while others say it can’t be done with a sealed copy.

It’s also worth noting that the US release specifically has a camouflaged pattern around the code, as shown by ResetEra user Mattmo831. That means you can certainly shine light into the box, but you can’t read the code on the other side.

Some PEGI units don’t have the camouflage pattern, so technically the code is visible using this trick, although again there’s still debate over whether the poster blocks the light in sealed copies.

It’s worth pointing out that codes aren’t activated at the point of purchase like other digital vouchers, so assuming the flashlight method works, it would be perfectly possible to pilfer a working copy of the game.

I think this story will explode if it turns out to be true, but it all just depends on how many PEGI copies don’t have the camouflage pattern and whether the inserted poster blocks the light or not.

As far as I can see, there aren’t an enormous number of people who’ve complained upon buying the physical version that their code has been redeemed – but if this method works, the publicity around it will now surely see the probability increase.

As the wait for Final Fantasy 14's new expansion Evercold presses on, Square Enix presents fans with a special promotion in preparation for the DLC – one that director and producer Naoki "Yoshi-P" Yoshida hopes will help tide the MMO's players over.

Unfortunately for all active Warriors of Light (hi, it's me), Evercold was recently hit with a four-week delay, pushing its long-awaited release date into February 2027. While that's not all that significant when compared to other games' own delays, it's still sort of a big deal for MMO players looking for new content to justify shelling out for a monthly subscription – and Yoshi-P knows it. That's where the Road to Evercold comes in. As he describes it in an online letter, it's "a way to encourage any Warrior of Light currently taking a break from their adventures to jump back into the fray before the new expansion arrives." He goes on to explain what prompted the Road to Evercold: "For MMORPGs – especially those with a monthly subscription fee – retaining active players is of utmost importance." So is bringing in new players.

"In addition to supporting our current players, it's vital that we also welcome new players into the fold, as well as ensure adventurers on a break can readily resume their journey." Neither of these tasks is easy, however, as the lead admits – but Yoshi-P notes, "We've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today."

And, yes, he's well-aware of the whole housing auto-demolition thing – but, again, it's not one of those "heavy-handed attempts" he mentions… it's "a symptom of the issues surrounding plots." As for what measures the developers are taking, "It's crucial that we run promotions to help those players toying with the idea of returning to Eorzea, and give them the tiny nudge they might need to dive back in," like the Road to Evercold.

In Yoshi-P's wise, wise words, "'Massively multiplayer' is at the heart of the MMORPG experience, which is precisely why doing our best to reach all of our Warriors of Light is our major focus." That's not to mention all of the changes Evercold is introducing. "With the theme of evolution at the forefront, we're expanding and adjusting systems, user interfaces, and content in a way we've never attempted before."

There's no better time to get back into the game if you're no longer in it, basically – and if you haven't been in it thanks to, uh, the ever-controversial Dawntrail… Well, that's where the whole Road to Evercold comes in, with the Mog Station's new optional $10 Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude item. It allows you to skip the main scenario from Patch 6.1, Newfound Adventure, through Patch 7.4, Into the Mist.

You do have to hit at least level 90, though, as Yoshi-P wants anyone who buys it to "be familiar with matching, and be well-experienced in battle." The hope here is "that players who have completed the game's first saga, but are currently taking a break, will seize this chance to see how FFXIV has evolved." I suppose I get it – Dawntrail suffered from "Mostly Negative" reviews for quite some time on Steam, after all.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

The Road to Evercold isn't just introducing a way to zoom past the MMO's least enticing content, either – it "features our longest Free Login Campaign to date," letting folks get back into the swing of things without breaking the bank. Part of me wishes there was some more in there to keep us occupied, but there's not all that long left until Evercold now anyway… plus, there's always Keyboard Brawler, which just got a nice little patch, too.

Final Fantasy 14 Evercold won't suffer from Dawntrail's pacing issues, Yoshi-P says, as the MMO commits to respecting your time.

#4059. Apex Legends adds a grumpy, teamwiping Godzilla to its growing history of unappealing crossovers

No doubt eager as peas to help pay off EA's billions in debt, battle royale shooter Apex Legends is set to run another of its intellectual propertytastic crossover events. This one, starting on November 10th, stars Godzilla, of Godzilla Minus Zero, Godzilla vs. Kong, Godzilla (1954), Godzilla 2000: Millennium, Godzilla (1998), Son of Godzilla, and Godzilla (2014). I might be missing some.

Besides a profitable range of weapon and character skins, most of which appear to have hot glue gunned an 70-year film franchise's worth of dorsal fins all over themselves, the King of the Monsters himself will show up on the game's Storm Point map. He does at least have more than a background cameo: he'll occasionally blast an area with Legend-melting atomic breath, though brave souls who risk the danger zone can score a custom Devotion LMG with a unique heat ray attack of its own.

Worth noting also that the character skins are each based on a certain 'zilla movie, though as our freelance news writer and associate Large Lizard Cinema expert Ashley isn't working today, I'm not sure which of these are from hits and which are the duds. Walking wallhack motherfucker Bloodhound gets the newest fashion, their skin being inspired by Minus Zero, while my personal favourite Scottish scientist Horizon gets duds based on Big G in Godzilla vs. Destoroyah. Octane's skin is taken from... something called a Jet Jaguar? Google suggests this may in fact be elite Godzilla knowledge, something I clearly lack.

Regardless, and with the understanding that a lot of effort goes into these crossovers, I still kinda wish they didn't exist? Even putting aside basic game-playing problems with how, for example, wacky skins interfere with Legend silhouettes – you couldn't pay me to initiate a fight against a full team of near-identical Gundampeople - it's just icky to have an otherwise sharp, smart, at times fiercely competitive battle royale turned into an animated billboard for a few days.

Besides, Apex already has its own kaiju: the sleepy, pacifist Leviathans that innocently wandered into the King's Canyon map for a few of the earlier seasons. I consider these much better Friend Material than Godzilla, on the grounds that they'd only kill you by accident, and it was usually your own fault - by wandering under their briefly raised megahooves - anyway.

#4058. YouTubers Share Their Amazing Home Videos From The Most Important Day In Xbox History

Happy birthday, Xbox! It's exactly 25 years today since the original Xbox console launched in North America on November 15th of 2001, and it turns out multiple people captured the moment via some amazing home video footage.

We've talked about one of these videos before — the ridiculously cool one from MyRetroLife, who has become a YouTube star since uploading his footage multiple years ago. His short clip of "booting up an original Xbox on launch day" has a whopping 4.6 million views, while his more elaborate story about it (which you can watch down below) has almost 900,000 views.

We're not affiliated with him, but you should go check out his other stuff as well - it's really entertaining!

It turns out there's more footage on YouTube from November 15th that we weren't aware of though, with this next example coming from The Great Gambino. They have much less of a high-profile following than MyRetroLife, but their three-minute Xbox footage is equally as interesting and nostalgic to watch, so it's well worth a view!

Apparently, this video was somewhat quietly uploaded to their YouTube channel a few years ago, but exploded into the millions of views after other people reposted it to the likes of TikTok, Facebook and other social media platforms.

They uploaded the most complete version of it a couple of years ago, which you can see below:

Of course, some of us Pure Xbox users were also there back on November 15th of 2001, unboxing our original Xbox consoles for the first time, but it's quite special to see the moment captured on camera for us to see in 2026!

There's more official footage of the OG Xbox launch out there as well if you go searching for it, but we reckon it's the home videos that paint a more accurate picture of what it was like to be an Xbox fan at the very beginning.

It's also the kind of thing that makes you realise how old you truly are!

Update: We've just come across another one! Here's an Xbox home video from thedanceman on YouTube:

#4057. "That Was Very Tough" - Indiana Jones Dev Struggled To Transition From Gunplay

Indiana Jones and the Great Circle is one of the biggest surprises in recent years. Developer MachineGames, well known for its ability to make gunning down Nazis immensely satisfying in its Wolfenstein franchise, created what is arguably the best Indy adventure since The Last Crusade.

Yet transitioning from Wolfenstein wasn't exactly easy for the studio. In a new interview with the FRVR podcast (thanks, VGC), design director Jens Andersson explains how the developers found it "very tough" to focus on melee combat, given its expertise in gunplay.

“It was one of those features that we were so afraid of. Especially since MachineGames’ pedigree of Wolfenstein, coming into making Indiana Jones with a team primed to make more gore with heavy weapons, running and gunning… and then ‘oh, we’re going to make a family-friendly adventure’. That was very tough.”

Granted, 'family-friendly' might be a bit of a stretch given the game's 16+ PEGI rating, but we understand the sentiment. To make matters worse, MachineGames had to nail the balance between making guns a last resort for Indy while ensuring they still felt good to use.

“That was non-negotiable because we have a lot of people at Machine that love guns. They love everything about guns. They have people that professionally compete shooting. Gun Nuts. Obviously, you know, from Wolfenstein games that interest has been satiated. And at the game time, you have so many fans of Quake and other shooters out there. So we can’t make gunplay bad, that wouldn’t have been acceptable.”

To ensure that fans of guns still enjoyed the game, MachineGames strived to make melee combat "interesting, fun, and easy". This, combined with making reloading a fairly slow process, encourages you to experiment with your environment and locate more melee weapons.

#4056. Sony boss says Spider-Man: Brand New Day should be nominated for Best Picture because there aren't 10 films better

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Can a superhero movie win Best Picture? Sony exec thinks so as Spider-Man: Brand New Day gears up to launch Oscars campaign

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As the best movies of the year gear up to campaign for the 99th Academy Awards, Sony Pictures boss is asking film fans to shine a light on Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

"The Academy is meant to recognize greatness. But also to receive wisdom about what greatness is," said the chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures in an interview with Deadline. "We’re gonna do what we can just to make people think about it. I think it’s also incumbent upon studios who make these kinds of quality commercial films to get people to think about it, and here’s what I ask people when I walk around: 'Are you telling me that there are 10 films this year that are better than this film?'"

Aside from Joaquin Phoenix taking home the gold for Best Actor in Joker and Heath Ledger winning the Oscar for Supporting Actor, superhero movies are often overlooked at the Oscars. An all-out comic book movie has never won Best Picture. But it looks like Sony Pictures is out to change that, as Marvel movie Spider-Man: Brand New Day is about to launch an all-out campaign to land a Best Picture nomination.

Of all the live-action Spider-Man movies, multiple entries have received nominations in the Visual Effects and Sound categories, but only Spider-Man 2 won Best Visual Effects in 2005. But times are changing, and so are movie-goers' appetites. This year, Brand New Day smashed all expectations, becoming the highest-grossing film ever in the US. The movie is also very relatable to many, raising important and rather pertinent issues of loneliness among young adults.

"I think Academy members would be interested in this because it’s very significant from a storytelling movie," continued Rothman. "This is really the first of these kinds of movies that I can think of that does not climax in a giant battle. In this movie, there is no giant action sequence at the end. The climax of this movie is two young people sitting on the edge of a bed, talking to each other and sharing their deepest pain. This movie is melancholy in that way and beautiful."

Tom Holland's fourth Spidey movie may also have more of a chance after the Academy moved the number of Best Picture nominations up to 10 in 2021, seemingly to include a wider range of movies. "Wise heads know that quality commercial filmmaking is extremely difficult," pointed out the Sony Exec, raising the question again, "are there 10 films that are better than this film, just in pure quality?"

For more, check out our guide on how to watch the Marvel movies in order, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies on the way.

#4055. The Legend of Khiimori's Mongolian Expanse update brings in frosty mountains and scorching deserts that'll require a lot more than a fur coat and a sturdy horse

Another day, another opportunity for some horsing around! I'm being literal here, to be clear, as a new update for The Legend of Khiimori dropped yesterday. It's called The Mongolian Expanse, opening up the map a whole lot more and making a sweep of other additions to the game.

Previously, you might have looked out unto the snowy mountainscapes and the scorching deserts and thought "boy howdy am I glad I can't go there, those temperatures look like a nightmare to deal with!" Well, good news, as you now can head to those locales, each with "their own waystations, Yam nodes, named places, chests and bandit caches."

You don't want to wander there without some amount of prep, however, as the mountains are cold and difficult to climb, with wolves none too kind to humans like you. The desert, of course, is really hot, for both you and your horse. Both additions remind me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its use of extreme temperatures acting as a sort of challenge gate. Neat stuff!

The buck doesn't stop there with this update though. You'll find a whole host of new wildlife, ranging from wild boars, to gobi bears and camels. Of course, a horse game wouldn't be one without more horse, which there is! It's a new breed called the Marwari, a horse that is "built for endurance and especially resistant to heat, a strong partner for long, punishing Desert crossings." Beyond that, you'll also find more than 60 new horse skills, all findable across specific regions and for specific breeds.

It's a nice beefy update with plenty more tweaks, additions and fixes on top of everything mentioned above. When it comes to the mountains and desert, you can also expect some big additions there, as this is only the first part of this update. You can read about everything else the update offers right here on Steam.

#4054. DokeV Set for 2028 Launch, But You'll See It Again This Year

But the Crimson Desert dev is embracing AI

Remember DokeV? The bizarre Pokémon-esque game announced over five years ago from Pearl Abyss? The developer has gone on to make Crimson Desert, but in a new financial report, it's shared its wild take on Pokémon is still coming.

Now its Charting the Unknown expansion for Crimson Desert is out, it's shifting more of its developers onto DokeV, and the firm is targeting a launch in the second half of 2028. Before the end of this year, however, it plans to reveal its latest "development progress".

DokeV was originally revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live in 2021, a show run by Geoff Keighley. There is a good chance the re-reveal of the game will take place next month at The Game Awards, then.

Here's that wacky announcement trailer as a reminder:

Having shown it again, Pearl Abyss will have hands-on demos in the second half of 2027. It said: "We will continue to communicate with players by sharing updates at optimal timing to effectively highlight the game's direction and core strengths."

The problem is it sounds like the developer is embracing more AI development to achieve that.

In the financial report, Pearl Abyss confirms that it's "integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality". AI is being used across "the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimisation", and its use is being expanded to the team's "entire development pipeline".

"This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed," it added.

News 'We Should Have Clearly Disclosed Our Use of AI': Crimson Desert Dev 'Sincerely Apologises' for Erroneously Including AI Art in PS5 Game

For now, though, the studio claims AI serves "strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity". Humans are still behind the "core gameplay experience and actual content creation".

Crimson Desert got into hot water shortly after its release for including AI portraits in some of its environments. It did remove them from the game and issued an apology where it said the assets were "unintentionally included in the final release. This is not in line with our internal standards, and we take full responsibility for it."

Now, as it looks to the future, Pearl Abyss seemingly plans to lean even more into AI development.

[source pearlabyss.com, via gamesradar.com]

#4053. Talking Point: As Xbox Celebrates Its 25th Anniversary, What Are Your Hopes For The Next 25 Years?

Maybe we'll be looking back on this in 2051!

The celebrations for Xbox's official 25th anniversary roll on! We've finally arrived at November 15th, which marks the exact date when the original Xbox launched all the way back in 2001. How time flies!

Of course, this is a great chance to reflect on everything that's happened over the past 25 years, which we've been doing in various articles throughout the month (and indeed the year), but it's also an opportunity to think about the next 25 years and where Xbox as a brand might be headed in the future.

I think the cynical view, and perhaps the logical view, is that Xbox won't exist by the time we get to 2051. Let's not forget that PlayStation was still in its infancy 25 years ago, SEGA had just got out of the console business after being a major player for so long, and Nintendo hadn't even released the GameCube in North America until November 18th of 2001.

Feature 25 Years Later, How Many Of These Original Xbox Launch Titles Have You Played?

From the original North American launch on November 15, 2001

In other words, 25 years is a very long time, and we've seen many ups and downs from Xbox throughout its history. The glory days of Halo, Xbox Live and the Xbox 360 were followed up by a horribly botched Xbox One launch, and the Xbox Series era has been summed up as everything from extremely promising to extremely disappointing, now hovering somewhere in the 'cautiously optimistic' territory for some Xbox fans since Asha Sharma took the helm earlier in 2026.

While console sales might be down, and the Xbox CEO keeps talking about a need to "return to growth", there's every reason to believe Xbox might still be a powerhouse in 25 years' time. Microsoft's backing is obviously a big aspect of that — assuming the brand never gets sold off — but so is the mountain of incredible first-party IP (Minecraft, Call of Duty, World of Warcraft, etc.) that should continue to rake in money over the next decade at least, coupled with the ability to innovate in the hardware space and eventually win back some market share with handhelds and consoles.

Realistically, the answer to all of this is that we don't have an answer - it's impossible to predict a future that's still 25 years out, especially when Xbox's mission statement appears to have changed on an almost yearly basis during the 2020s. There's no doubt that Xbox will face many challenges in the 25 years that are ahead and it'll be forced to adapt and innovate along the way, but I wouldn't be surprised if we're still talking about it in 2051!

For what it's worth, here's what Xbox boss Asha Sharma said on this topic a few days ago:

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this. [..] A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

Talking Point As Xbox Celebrates 25 Years, What's Your First Ever Xbox Memory?

News Asha Sharma Issues Statement On Xbox's 25th Anniversary And The Future Of Gaming

If you don't feel berated enough in Ocarina of Time, you can now add a full-size fairy to watch judgmentally from the shelf because a fan just made their own version of Lego Navi.

The finished product was posted over at Reddit by AdatheB, and it's instantly recognizable as Link's fairy companion. Presumably made using spare parts of a kind you'd find on Lego's Pick a Brick store page, their Lego Navi figure is around six to seven inches tall and 'floats' on a clear stand. It's also the closest we're likely to get to a full-size kit, because as of right now the only official model is a tiny stud Navi in the Ocarina of Time Final Battle set (available at Amazon) and the now-retired Deku Tree, AKA one of the best Lego sets.

As the post's top comment from CommunicationSea3329 says, "Lego should listen to your idea."

This isn't the first time AdatheB has created their own gaming-themed Lego set; in a reply on the same Reddit thread, they show off their full shelves where Navi now lives, and it features figures like a Hollow Knight kit and multiple Lego Pikmin. With that in mind, I think the above comment is right, and Nintendo should start following AdatheB's example. I'd love to have a Pikmin set perched above my Switch, for instance.

In the here and now, this fan-made kit stands out because, generally speaking, there's not much actual Navi merch. The best you can usually expect is third-party gear like keychains (such as this unnamed-but-clearly-Navi one at Amazon) or earrings. However, with the popularity of the Ocarina of Time remake, I wouldn't be surprised to see more in the not-so-distant future.

Still hoping to buy the Hori Ocarina of Time? Our guide should help you out. We've also got a roundup of the best Legend of Zelda merch there is, not to mention a breakdown of where to buy the Hasbro Master Sword.

#4051. After a 16-year long dev period, Faraway, a shooting star arcade game about siphoning the energy of other stars, is out now

Lord almighty, video games take a while to make, 'ey? Especially if you're just one person working on it by yourself. Such is the case with Faraway, out today, an arcade game that reminds me of the early days of PS3 indies "about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive," all made single-handedly by creator of cult-classic mobile game Eliss, Steph Thirion. Did I mention that Faraway took 16 years to make? Like I said, game development is a lengthy process.

Looking at Faraway, and knowing how long it took to produce, it doesn't surprise me to come from a dev who managed to release a mobile game in the early days of the platform, long before free-to-play got its chokehold on the industry. It also really does feel like it should be sitting amongst the likes of PixelJunk, this thing should be something I'm desperate to play on my PS3 while I wait for my controller to charge.

As mentioned, you are a shooting star, a "spark meant to shine and vanish in a blink." But still you persist, connecting to and wrapping yourself around starts to "harvest their energy," in turn lengthening your own life, and of course, in arcadey fashion, racking up a nice score. It looks like game design as poetry, everything you're looking at procedurally generated to bring freshness to every run. I can fully envision this as a "one more run" kind of arcade game, the best kind, especially in an age long past the need to shove in another of your hard earned coins.

Faraway conceptually charms me because it taps into a style of game we don't get to see much of any more. What I'm saying is, I'm just a teensy bit sick of how many roguelikes there are, but that doesn't mean I don't want a game I can just hop in and out of at my own whims. Sure, arcade games might not be in vogue, I just miss them a bit. In any case, Faraway is available to pick up on Steam right now. Seems like it'll be worth a punt!

#4049. Ablahshikar is a maximalist, sickos only salvage-survival CRPG about ripping organs out of warships and pawning off strange goods that's now out in early access

I don't know what's going on, and I like it

Sometimes, you come across a game and instantly know it's for the sickos. Today that is Ablahshikar, a "turn-based salvage-survival CRPG adrift on the Candle Sea" where you rip out the organs of enemy warships to "rebuild your vessel into a doomed chimera," that is out now in early access. To be honest I could have just called it a CRPG and still labelled it as a game for sickos, yet everything that's going on here is obviously just doubling down on the sick factor.

Ablahshikar is a particular flavour of maximalism. Having not played it, it feels a bit impossible describe, I mean, just have a read of some of the game's Steam page: "Lo, destiny crooks a finger only to those whose eyes peer beyond þe next tempest. Take custody of a faltering war-barge that wanders the outer brine of Dastgerd. Thy wrists y-braced to a wan terminal of bone-whyte and tarnysshed latoun, þou steerest Ablahshikar by murke point-nettes and sputteryng tables." I don't know what any of that means! And I love it. Reminds me of Hylics in that the game's world is not translating itself for its audience; you take what you're given, and you figure it out yourself.

Judging from trailers and screenshots, there's a mix of activities to be getting on with. Occasionally you'll be piloting a strange, not alien, but definitely ancient ship of some kind in an arcadey sort of fashion. Then occasionally there's something that resembles Caves of Qud, i.e. some odd, 2D maybe dungeon crawling where your moves are dictated by individual keys on your keyboard. Then there's Disco Elysiumy cutscenes that feel like a video game designed in the year 1200 by someone from the year 2200, aesthetically anyway. As I said, it is a particular flavour of maximalism.

Truthfully, I do not know if I am sicko enough for Ablahshikar. Its mighty vision is terrifying, but I certainly am curious about it. Right now it's less than a fiver, and it'll only be in early access for roughly a couple of months where the price will then go up, so perhaps it's best to get in at the ground floor. If you are one such sicko, then you can pick it up on Steam right here.

#4048. The Excellent Warhammer Survivors Reveals Roadmap Full of Free Updates, Teases Something Big

Warhammer Survivors launched just a few days ago, and I think it's an absolutely fantastic take on the criminally addictive Vampire Survivors formula.

Imagine my glee, then, to learn that developer Auroch Digital has big plans for the game going forward.

The Bristol-based studio has revealed a chunky content roadmap that leads into next year — and there's some really good stuff on the way.

It all starts with a major update that's landing in December. It'll bring new characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions to the already packed release.

Another two admittedly lesser but still welcome updates are expected in January; one promises quality of life improvements — which is interesting in itself — and the other will add cross-save functionality, so you can carry your progress between multiple platforms.

After that, a second major update drops in early 2027. Like the one that's expected in December, this patch flushes the game with yet more new characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions. You'd best get grinding before then!

And finally, at some point in the second quarter of next year, there's going to be a "larger piece of content". I'm guessing this'll be some sort of DLC or expansion; as of right now, Auroch Digital's teasing it and nothing more.

"We have been blown away by the support of Warhammer Survivors since launch, and we want to share our appreciation for everyone who has played the game so far," the developer writes.

Are you blasting your way through Warhammer Survivors right now? Ask the Emperor for aid in the comments section below.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A lead developer on Xbox Project Helix says that rising hardware costs are a primary driver of the upcoming console's development.

As part of the console brand's 25th anniversary, Microsoft has released a magazine about Xbox's past, present, and future. This online magazine includes an interview with Jason Ronald, vice president of next-generation console development at Microsoft and the lead for Project Helix. In this interview, he clarifies that Xbox Project Helix is "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," rather than the other way around.

Obviously, the biggest conversations about the Xbox Project Helix – and the PS6 – are cost. Hardware prices are rising thanks to the ongoing global RAM shortages brought on by AI companies who just need to let your weird uncle generate what he looks like as a Simpson to post on Facebook. The Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and Nintendo Switch 2 have all had price increases over the past year, but Ronald says keeping the price down is a crucial motivator in the console's design.

"It's definitely a challenging time," Ronald says, adding, "it’s also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable."

He explains the cost factor is why the team behind Project Helix is "really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it’s an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that."

Obviously AI-assisted tech was a big talking point within games before the memory crisis, but it feels like it's only going to become more prominent. Sony has been implementing QSSR frame generation tech into its PS5 games, likely in part because nobody can afford a PS5 Pro now that it's almost $1,000.

And with things going like they are, it's probably going to be the norm heading forward… let's just hope Xbox puts its money where its mouth is and actually makes the Helix affordable. But given the current rumor is it's going to be $1,800, I'm not too hopeful.

#4046. BioWare are gone, but at least you'll be able to watch their final days in a documentary next year and oh wait that's really sad actually

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

In a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again."

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.

#4045. Shigeru Miyamoto To Receive The Inaugural 'Legend Award' At The 30th D.I.C.E. Awards

Award will be presented only once per decade

The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) has announced that Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of iconic Nintendo franchises like Super Mario and The Legend of Zelda, will receive the inaugural Legend Award at the upcoming 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on Thursday, 18th February 2027.

The award, which will only be presented once per decade, 'recognises an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment'. It's designed to honour creators whose achievements have already earning lasting universal acclaim, while celebrating their 'immeasurable impact and influence'.

Meggan Scavio, President of the AIAS, said the following:

“Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards."

Though his current focus is on the production of movies and theme parks, Miyamoto-san is arguably the most recognisable figure in Nintendo's history, and it's difficult to imagine whether the company would even exist today without his creations.

He most recently appeared during a Pikmin Day Direct presentation, during which he revealed a new demo for Pikmin 4 on Switch 2 along with some Pikmin Bloom updates and the commencement of monthly Hello! Pikmin movies on the Nintendo Today app.

#4044. 'The Ultimate Gaming Machine' - Xbox Reveals Tons Of New Project Helix Information

Also clarifying that it's definitely a console and not a PC

As part of Xbox's 25th anniversary celebrations today, we've been treated to a new digital version of a magazine that was given out at Seattle FanFest earlier this week, available to read in full over on the official Xbox Wire website.

The bit that's getting most attention concerns Xbox Project Helix - the new next-gen console that's currently in the works over at Xbox HQ. The brand's VP of Next Generation, Jason Ronald, shares tons of new information across four pages in the magazine, helping to give us a better idea of what to expect from the upcoming console.

There's one section in particular that's getting all the interest on social media right now, where he clarifies that Project Helix is definitely a console that can play PC games, and definitely not a PC that happens to play console games.

"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Beyond this, Ronald talks in depth about loads of other aspects of what they're aiming for with Project Helix, and as mentioned, there's so much detail that it spreads across four pages of the magazine.

In the interest of highlighting as much as possible though, we thought we'd transcribe all of most notable quotes from the magazine down below, whereas you can read the added context inside of the magazine article itself.

Here are more of the key bits from the magazine article:

"When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine - one that removes all barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games."

"We don't think the next generation is defined by 8K or 240 hertz, or some of the traditional metrics - it's really about gameplay innovation. It's about deeper immersion. It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering, to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

"When I think about what makes a console magical, it's that it just makes my games instantly accessible and ready to play in an instant. I don't have to worry about updating my operating system, updating drivers, configuring different settings - things like that. The hardware and the experience is entirely designed around playing games."

"The very first next-generation conversations we had were with all of our first-party studios. That was absolutely foundational to the design of what we've done with Project Helix - talking about where they saw the future of game design going, where they saw the future of their franchises going, and what was constraining their creative ambition."

"With Xbox One, I think we got so focused on expanding our aperture that we lost sight of what truly is magical, which is players, developers, and the games that they love. We have to build the best platform for game developers to deliver their creative vision."

"The other thing, and I think this is something that is unique about Xbox, is we have to be connected to the community. A lot of the features that people have come to love and expect from Xbox have actually been driven directly by community feedback. I think that's really core to the soul of who Xbox is, because if you're in touch with your player base, you never go wrong if you focus on what their needs are."

"It's definitely a challenging time, but as a system and a platform designer, it's also one of the most exciting times, because we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable."

"This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

"The ROG Xbox Ally was really an opportunity for us to learn alongside our player base with a lot of these concepts and the ideas that we had: being able to play libraries from across multiple different storefronts, understanding how PC games and console games can show up together in a unified library. The feedback that we've gotten from players has fundamentally informed and altered our plans of how it actually shows up in a future console. Players shared where we met the mark and areas we needed to improve or approach differently. So absolutely, we view the Ally as a precursor to what we're doing with Helix - but it's informed by a lot of the design concepts we have for Helix."

Sorry for the wall of quotes, but we thought you might find all of this pretty interesting! It's not even the full extent of what Ronald had to say, as he also touched on the importance of game preservation to the Xbox platform in general, as well as how Project Helix will seemingly have a bespoke UI, but one that still feels familiar to Xbox fans.

Of course, we're still waiting on concrete details about what Helix will look like, how much it'll cost, how significant the PC integration will be, and loads of other things that will give us a much better picture of how it'll shape up.

It seems like we won't be getting that this year though, and if rumours are to be believed, Xbox might even be releasing a first-party handheld in 2027 before the Project Helix console in 2028. Who knows... plans can always change.

For now, let us know what you think about this latest info on Xbox Project Helix down below, and we definitely recommend reading the full Xbox 25th anniversary magazine for yourself - we wish we could buy one to be honest!

I'd like to know whether it has a disc-drive because I have an extensive Blu-ray film collection (2000+ films), and I currently use my Series X to play them. I'm not fussed about the capability to play physical games because I have been all digital since the beginning of the Xbox One era. If it does not come with a disc-drive, then one that can be added (much like with the PS5) would be good. It's not a deal breaker for me because I can always just buy a 4K Blu-ray player, but it would be better to have just Helix and a PS6 under my television, rather than a Blu-ray player as well.

I have a gaming PC that I do not use for gaming right now, so all I really want is for Helix to be a console that is more powerful than the Series X I already own. I want the simplicity of console gaming, not the complexity that PC gaming often brings.

Does it allow access to other storefronts?:

I have said so many times that I think Xbox allowing store fronts like Steam on Helix would be a massive mistake. Once people realise that even brand new games on Steam often cost £10 less upon release than they do on Xbox, and once they see how games are cut more deeply in sales on Steam than they are on consoles, they will soon begin to make Steam their dominant library, and that will cost Microsoft billions in lost revenue, and given how Xbox is doing right now, that could easily sound the death knell for Xbox. Xbox needs to be making more money, not losing more still by enabling consumers to buy their games on Steam etc..

The only other thing that I would like an answer to right now is when Helix will launch. Rumour has it that the PS6 will release next year, and if the other rumour doing the rounds about Helix releasing in 2028 is true, then Helix will sink without a trace unless it is massively more powerful than the PS6, and considerably cheaper than it too. Helix needs to release at the same time as the PS6, or preferably a year before it, for it to stand a chance of success, particularly if Helix is basically a console because then that does mean that both the PS6 and Helix could be more or less on par in terms of power. As a PC, then it was always expected that Helix would be considerably more powerful than the PS6, but if both are consoles, then they may be much closer to one another in terms of power, which will probably favour PlayStation given the current userbase imbalance. It's going to be a difficult balancing act for Xbox when it comes to power and capabilities versus pricing, and how that stacks up to the PS6, but whatever happens, I really do not think that Helix can allow the PS6 a years head start.

Those are the three biggest questions that I have for Helix. I'm not overly concerned about the price because I want Helix to be my primary gaming platform even though I will be buying a PS6 too. With any luck, we will hear a lot more details within the next 6 months (unless Helix is releasing in 2028, in which case it'll be more like 18 months)...

@Sol4ris Absolutely ! Xbox Helix will almost certainly be superior to the PS6. That's already pretty obvious in terms of power, the size of its game library, its services, the technologies it offers, and the level of freedom it provides, such as game modding.

At this point, the main advantage PlayStation may have left is price. We'll see whether the difference is significant or not, but considering Helix's advantages, if the price gap isn't huge, it will probably be well worth spending a bit more for a Helix.

There's also the battle over exclusive games. Xbox is expected to launch Helix with a strong lineup of exclusive titles, and the PS6 will likely do the same. But when you really think about it, even on that front PlayStation may already be at a disadvantage, since roughly 30-40% of the games available on Helix could be console exclusives to the platform, including not only Xbox first-party titles but also all the games that are released exclusively on PC, and there are a lot of those. Of course, that's talking about quantity and variety, which are already important advantages. The remaining question is game quality. And on that front, PlayStation needs to raise its game, because lately its first-party exclusives have not only been relatively few in number, but also haven't always lived up to expectations.

The next console war will also be decided by marketing and the public perception of the two brands. In that respect, PlayStation's reputation has taken quite a hit, while Xbox's image has become increasingly positive, particularly since Asha Sharma's arrival and the introduction of numerous player-friendly initiatives, such as Xbox Play Anywhere, lower Game Pass pricing, disc-to-digital support, a renewed focus on exclusive games, a stronger emphasis on consoles, the Rewards program, backward compatibility, and more.

These are all areas that distinguish Xbox from PlayStation, which, in comparison, doesn't seem to do much for its community other than ignore it.

I 100% believe (I cannot be any more categorical than that, can I) that having Steam on Helix will be the biggest blunder that Microsoft have ever made, and let's face it, they have had some doozies!

I think that yes, having Steam on Helix will see the console sell more units, but how many of those that buy it will be looking to use it as an entry point into PC gaming, not as an Xbox? Microsoft would only make whatever small profit they add to the price of Helix itself, but once that unit has been sold, they will see not a penny more. Of course, if Microsoft subsidise it, and people then just use it as an entry point into PC gaming then Microsoft will be making a loss on each Helix and gaining nothing from the Xbox side of things. It is for that reason that I suspect Helix will not be subsided (if it is a PC) as the whole point of subsidising a console in the first place is to make the selling price attractive enough to entice people into your ecosystem. If there is a risk that people will not enter the Xbox ecosystem, then I think Microsoft will decide to forgo subsidising Helix, unless they calculate that the number of people who would just use it as a Steam machine is negligible. I know one thing for certain, I would not want to be the one making that decision!

Problem is, I think even amongst the Xbox faithful, there will be many that are drawn to the cheaper games that can be found on Steam, and let's not forget, that is before we take into consideration that if you buy a game on Steam you do not need to pay a subscription in order to game online either. Personally, I think the temptation to move away from Xbox will be too great for a decent percentage of Xbox gamers. After all, they would have the best of all worlds; an entry point PC that enables them to play their historic Xbox games library, and also a cheaper store that offers more content, and no need to pay for online play. What's not to like?

Indeed, if Xbox thinks they have money woes now (and they do, let's be honest, as there is no other reason to be downsizing, cancelling games, making developers redundant and selling off studios), then wait until the 💩 really hits the fan when people stop buying games on the Xbox Store and buy from Steam instead. If enough people do that, then Xbox could be mortally wounded.

Truth is, I like the sound of a Helix that offers me console like gaming, access to my extensive Xbox games library, and Steam all rolled into one, but I really think it will spell trouble for Xbox, which is why in the long run, I would prefer Steam was off the table.

I still think Roland left wriggle room when it comes to other storefronts when he could have excited the Xbox community still further by explicitly confirming that Steam was included. However, he didn't, and instead suggested 'alterations', which could of course mean absolutely anything from a change of UI, a change in the way we would access these other storefronts, or indeed no other storefronts at all.

I will be getting Helix, of that there is no doubt, and I will primarily (I think) be using at as an Xbox console because that is all I really want as I already have a top-notch gaming PC, thus have no need for another one...

#4043. Poll: Are You Hyped for November's 10 New PS Plus Games?

I don't want to influence your opinion right out of the gate here, but November's PS Plus Extra lineup will surely go down as one of the service's strongest offerings in recent memory.

It's got a bit of everything, but it's also packed with highly rated titles. Death Stranding 2: On the Beach was a Game of the Year contender just 12 months back — a madcap but heartfelt sequel to Kojima Productions' impressively unique 'strand-type' debut.

And while Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii is far from being peak Yakuza, it's still a damn fun and endearingly stupid spin-off. Well worth checking out if you're looking for something a little less serious, without sacrificing the dramatic storytelling that the franchise is known for.

Elsewhere, Atomfall is a bit like if Fallout was set in rural England, and Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake is old school JRPG bliss brought into the modern era.

We've even got two completely different shooters up for grabs: Trepang2 is an unhinged run-and-gunner with horror elements, and Hell Let Loose is a grounded World War 2 reenactment for up to 100 players.

You could probably argue that PS Plus Premium's having an uncharacteristically decent month as well. Soul Reaver 2 is an absolutely lore-soaked sequel to the beloved PS1 action adventure, and Freedom Wars Remastered gives one of the Vita's best action RPGs a welcome second chance.

News 10 PS Plus Extra, Premium Games for November 2026 Announced

Skydance hasn't seen the Superman sequel yet

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Despite being ousted from DC Studios in the wake of Skydance Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros., James Gunn has still found time to debunk rumors about the status of upcoming Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow.

Writing on Threads – where else? – Gunn stated, "There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made."

The ex-DC Studios co-CEO added, "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are [fellow ex-co-CEO] Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false."

Whispers had circulated that Skydance would be getting more hands-on with Man of Tomorrow as its new DCU vision began to take shape.

In early November, Gunn and Safran stepped down as heads of DC Studios, with one-time Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham taking over from December 1. In a statement, Gunn admitted he was "incredibly relieved to get back to pure filmmaking" but little is known at this current juncture about what will happen with the overall vision put forth by Gunn as part of DCU Chapter One: Gods and Monsters.

Man of Tomorrow, meanwhile, features a who's who of the DCU, including David Corenswet, Nicholas Hoult, Rachel Brosnahan, Edi Gathegi, Nathan Fillion, Milly Alcock, Aaron Pierre, and Xolo Mariduena. Matthew Lillard is also in the cast, with the actor confirming he will play an original character not found in the comic books.

Man of Tomorrow hits cinemas on July 9, 2027. For more, we have a guide to upcoming superhero movies.

#4041. Take on a time-manipulating corporation in the very Soul Eater meets Jet Set Radio action roguelite CHRONO PUNK

Plus a little bit of Spider-Man, Devil May Cry and Kingdom Hearts

My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from said era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are big and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

#4040. After taking over EA, Saudi Arabia and their private equity cronies have reportedly held talks about buying Unity

The engine builders have, it's claimed, been working with an investment ​bank to evaluate [their] options

Members of the consortium led by the Saudi Arabian government's Public Investment Fund and some private equity suits which took over EA this year in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion reportedly have a new target in their sights. Unity, software company and makers of the game engine bearing the same name, have held talks with the consortium over a potential takeover, it's claimed.

According to Reuters, a consortium including Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and private equity firm Silver Lake Partners recently approached Unity about a deal that would value the company at around $25 billion. Unity are, it's claimed, currently working with an investment bank to evaluate their options following the chat, with no deal set in stone right now.

Silver Lake, Reuters note, are already among Unity's largest shareholders and invested up to $400 million in the engine builders in 2017. In fact, Silver Lake's managing director and CEO Egon Durban already has a seat on Unity's board of directors, so will probably have to butt out of any takeover talks.

Assuming the consortium would go the leveraged buyout route, loading Unity up with debt like the EA takeover did, it's hard to see any deal not resulting in similarly catastrophic consequences for those working at Unity. EA laid off a reported 400 people in an effort to cut costs after coming under the boot of the Saudi state and private equity, shutting BioWare and cancelling something Sims-related codenamed Project Lotus. BioWare's demise has since been reported to have largely come down to EA execs not wanting to fund both Star Wars Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, with them opting to back only Battlefront 3.

Unity's recent financial results are looking strong, propped up by year-on-year growth in an AI-powered ad network dubbed Vector, so one would assume that bit of the business likely wouldn't be top of the list if any bloodletting was to end up happening.

Solidarity to any Unity workers who're now having to live under the shadow of this prospective takeover and the upheaval it could lead to if it goes ahead in a fashion which mirrors the EA deal.

#4039. NBA 2K27 Brings A Slice Of GTA 6's Vice City To Switch 2 This Month

A little-known curio called Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching this week; you may have heard of it. It's not releasing on Switch 2, of course, but that doesn't prevent any crossover content from making it our way. And so, welcome to the closest we'll get to GTA 6 on Switch 2, via NBA 2K27, of all places.

2K has just announced the forthcoming season of 2K27's online The City game mode, which'll feature an official crossover with Rockstar and GTA 6. Season 3 is all about Vice City, with Rockstar's already infamous take on the Miami streets making its way into online hooping sessions.

The season kicks off on 27th November, and includes a new Vice City-inspired Park and a bunch of new clothing and accessory items for your MyPlayer, like Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, and Burger Shot and Cluckin’ Bell Employee Outfits.

Here's a handful of screenshots of the event — none of which come from the Switch 2 version, obviously:

The open 'The City' mode is available in NBA 2K27 on Switch 2 (after the console missed out on the larger space in previous entries), though 2K still hasn't graced the hybrid with crossplay, so expect things to still be very quiet.

2K is marking the occasion with the digital release of the NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition on 27th November. This one features Miami Heat's own Bam Adebayo on the cover, and comes bundled with a handful of extra perks (Season 3 Pro Pass, Vice City T-Shirt, 30 Skill Boosts, and 15 Gatorade Boosts).

So no, we won't be diving into GTA 6 on our Switch 2s any time soon, but hey, this is... something?

James Gunn may have been ousted from DC, but Chris Pratt wants him back at Marvel

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After James Gunn was surprisingly ousted from DC, Star-Lord actor Chris Pratt is open to the director returning to Marvel.

Gunn was previously co-CEO of DC Studios, but news broke recently that he and his co-CEO Peter Safran were out following the Paramount and Warner Bros. merger to create Skydance.

"That would be awesome," Pratt told Moviezine of the possibility of Gunn returning to Marvel. "I love working with James. He's the man. I haven't had the chance to speak with him since that news came out… it's always tough because anytime something like this comes up it could always become a headline."

He added: "All I'll say is I love James. He directed all three movies, and that's pretty rare… so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, I would love that."

There's no word on what might be next for Gunn, including whether that might be more DC projects. All that's known for sure is that Gunn is no longer shepherding the DCU.

Gunn has also recently debunked rumors that Skydance has seen the upcoming Man of Tomorrow and wants changes.

"There are a lot of untrue rumors going around, but one of them is that Skydance has seen Man of Tomorrow and that all sorts of sweeping changes are being made," Gunn wrote on Threads. "No one from Skydance has even seen the movie – the only people that have are Peter Safran and a very small trusted group of friends and family. So any stories around this narrative are false."

Man of Tomorrow arrives on July 9, 2027, and, while it's a follow-up to 2025's Superman, it's not strictly a sequel.

As for Marvel, Avengers: Doomsday lands on December 18. While you wait, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else the MCU has in store.

#4037. Rumour: Rainbow Six: Vegas 3 Now in the Works at Ubisoft

Ubisoft has just greenlit and entered the early stages of development on a third Rainbow Six: Vegas game, according to a new Insider Gaming report.

The outlet, which seems to have been clued up on internal Ubisoft happenings for years, claims the new entry is one of three projects that have just started production at Ubisoft Montreal, and one of the other two is also set in the Rainbow Six universe.

That's according to sources speaking under anonymity to the website.

While the Rainbow Six name is still used to this day, most notably in Rainbow Six: Siege, the Vegas sub-series stopped in 2008, after the release of Rainbow Six: Vegas 2. This reported third instalment enters development 18 years later.

Sources discussing the matter with Insider Gaming suggest the project is most likely Vegas 3, and not a remake of the previous entries. It's apparently very early in development, though, so don't expect a public reveal for a number of years — that is if it doesn't get cancelled before then.

#4036. "It's a brave new world": GTA 6's PC port will release sooner than you think to avoid losing money to AI rip-offs, says former Rockstar tech director

"If it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it."

GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it launches on 19th November. In general, Vermeij thinks that how to avoid having your games duplicated by chatbot herders is "the big question" right now for devs and publishers, particularly those who don't have the means to enforce their intellectual property dominions as vehemently as Take-Two do for Grand Theft Auto.

Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved. He shared a sweary anecdote about the company's difficulties getting the original GTA 1 to look the business on Sony's PlayStation.

"I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the company at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he said. "So they worked on PC and then an external company in Dundee did the PlayStation version. Which was really weird, because like, PCs were so much more powerful - still the case, but in those days, it was even more so.

"And I remember, at the time, the GTA team was definitely the most rowdy of all of the teams," Vermeij continued. "And there was one particular day where they sent the PC build away, and then it came back from the PlayStation people, and they had cut down all the textures from 256 colours to 16 colours, and my god, the artist was just going around and swearing - 'what the fuck did they do to our textures, I can't believe it, we can't release this shite'. So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console. So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better."

When it came time to develop GTA 3, Rockstar "flipped that around", Vermeij went on, creating the console versions first. "Clearly the PC market has sort of grown, caught up with the console market, but there's still that same mindset," he said. Most publishers prefer to release all versions at once, Vermeij added, "because then there's only one marketing campaign they have to pay for." GTA lives by its own rules, however. "I guess it's less of an argument for them because the game is just so big, so they just kind of always left it that way. And for developers, it's way easier to just do one version at a time. So, you know, that makes sense."

The arrival of generative AI threatens to throw all this to the winds. Tools such as Reverse Engineer Anything allow for speedy unofficial ports or "slopcomps" of console games on PC, despite warnings from seasoned recomp developers that using genAI for this purpose wrecks the community aspect of unofficial porting, and results in illegible "bruteforce" code rather than preserving some understanding of how the original game was made.

"It really has changed the world," Vermeij observed, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

GTA 6 is, according to Rockstar and Take-Two at least, an enormously fiddly production, costing hundreds of millions of dollars over eight years in development. Nonetheless, Vermeij thinks current genAI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a port. "It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things. And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it."

There are already signs that genAI PC port goldrushers are ready to pounce on GTA 6. Just today, Ars Technica reported on efforts to yassify the game's PS5 trailer footage by piping it through a stronker PC graphics card and using Nvidia's DLSS 5 to apply extra layers of gloss.

Vermeij himself left Rockstar way back in 2009 and is now an indie developer. His current early access project is Plentiful, a hexagonal god sim with an emphasis on water physics. It uses "AI-assisted machine translation for localization", but not for "gameplay content, art, or audio". Vermeij is, in general, interested in generative AI despite the surging tide of slopcomp ports. Smaller indie developers are, of course, more vulnerable to the financial fallout from having their work unofficially cloned by generative AI, but Vermeij thinks it's an existential worry for megacorps like Take-Two as well.

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest," he told me in closing. "I don't see it. But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you said, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job. But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out."

The latest rumour-mongering places GTA 6's PC release sometime in early 2027. In other news, Rockstar staff are soon to formally vote on whether to apply for union recognition. If the organisers carry the day, the resulting union could encompass nearly all the company's UK staff below management level.

#4034. Steam gets a boatload of restored Wing Commanders and Ultima ports after EA producer stumbles across cupboard of old tapes

"He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones"

EA have stuck a bunch of restored versions and ports of classic games, on Steam, GOG and the EA App. 25 games in all, including multiple entries in the Wing Commander and Ultima series, are part of the haul. Why's this happening now? Well, an EA producer stumbled across a cupboard full of old tapes, film reels and CDs.

According to an interview with The Game Business, the discovery of this old gubbins was a consequence of EA senior producer Jim Vessella needing somewhere new to stick a bunch of Betacam tapes used to help make the Command & Conquer Remastered Collection. "One of the facilities people was like, 'I think there’s a room in the other building that has a couple of items like that'," Vessella recalled. "He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones… just, whoa. Knowing what I’d discovered with the Command & Conquer tapes, I really felt like we had to find out what was on all these tapes."

The producer was able to convince EA's bosses that this stuff was worth the work needed to stick it back on storefronts, and lo, an EA blog post gushing about their vault's door having slid aside to reveal this pile of retro games. The collection includes restored versions of the following games, all with "robust quality-of-life updates and higher resolution Full-Motion Videos (FMV) from the Master tapes":

Meanwhile, the rest of the lineup is filled out by "faithful ports" of the following:

On Steam, all of these are currently on sale for less than a fiver each, with the prices of the most expensive ones set to rise to just under £10 when the introductory offer expires on November 19th.

It's good news in preservation terms, though I'm not sure it totally washes away the bad vibes of EA's Saudi and private equity owners reportedly looking to take over Unity.

The Dark Lord has been upgraded from 'giant eyeball' (or sexy Sauron, if we're talking Rings of Power) to 'the galaxy's fastest hunk of junk', because now he's a Lego Millennium Falcon.

Posted to reddit by fan builder Minute_Food_2881, this alternate design takes the Lego Sauron's Helmet set (widely available at the usual suspects like Amazon) and reforges it into the most iconic ship in Star Wars. There's no cheating here; no extra pieces are used for this Lego Millennium Falcon beyond what's in the box. Considering how accurate and convincing the final product is, that makes this spin on one of the best Lego sets even more impressive - a bit like the fan-made Lego Navi set that's also doing the rounds this week.

In terms of the kit used for this build, the Dark Lord's signature helmet is a pretty manageable build; it's only 13 inches tall and 538 pieces. Because it's $69.97 via Amazon (a fraction of the price many Lord of the Rings sets reach), this is amongst the cheapest Lego options for fans of Middle-earth right now.

Thanks to the gray of Sauron's helmet along with its blend of sharp lines and curves, it translates surprisingly well to being a Millennium Falcon. Minute_Food_2881's design is instantly recognizable as Han Solo's ship as a result, and it's reminiscent of the official midi-scale Lego Millennium Falcon.

The idea of turning something into Star Wars' most memorable bag of bolts is a long-running joke at this point (lovingly named "Can it Falcon?"), and there have been numerous amusing examples. It turns out that you can indeed turn a Lego pumpkin into the Millennium Falcon, for instance, and just last month someone made the ship from a chicken kit.

Not that the only cool sets from a galaxy far, far away are unofficial, of course. The new 50th anniversary Lego Star Wars sets are great, but I’m most interested in their weird collectible minifigures based on original concept art. Indeed, there are quite a few launching in January so it feels like 2027 could be a big one for fans of the franchise…

Because the franchise is celebrating a big birthday next year, there's plenty to get excited about; Hasbro goes back to the beginning with nostalgic Star Wars 50th anniversary action figures, for example.

#4032. Rumour: Atlus May Be Gearing Up For A Huge Persona 6 Reveal

After what felt like an age waiting for the Persona franchise to make its Switch debut, Sega and Atlus are now all-in on the Switch 2. Persona 4 Revival is scheduled to launch on 20th May 2027, while Persona 6 has also been confirmed for the hybrid console.

Atlus is in full marketing mode for Persona 4 Revival, but our pals over at Push Square have reason to believe that the company may be gearing up to properly reveal Persona 6 in the coming weeks.

This comes from Reddit user ronakwya, who notes that Atlus recently updated the official website for Persona 6. Apparently, however, this was the kind of update that allows Atlus to perform significant changes to the website in preparation for a big public reveal.

Ronakwya has also pointed to the gameplay reveal of Persona 4 Revival as a potential hint. Its own website was also updated in a similar manner roughly one month prior to its big reveal at the Xbox Games Showcase in June 2026.

So, which big gaming event is taking place in just less than a month from now..? Yep, The Game Awards 2026.

This all seems incredibly convenient though, and to be honest we're a little sceptical. As pointed out by Push Square, it would make little sense for Atlus to pull attention away from Persona 4 Revival at this stage to host a full reveal for Persona 6.

In our opinion, we could definitely see a similar reveal during the Xbox Games Showcase in 2027 after the release of Revival in May (February for other platforms). We're happy to be wrong, as we're proper itching to see some gameplay from the next mainline entry, but we're not holding our breath.
